**Finding: missing** (TRANSITION) — validated redline submitted.

**What I found.** The Agreement's only exit machinery is section 4(c) (p0019–p0022), which covers four things: Kubient ceases the Services, the section 3 license is revoked, Customer stops using the Services/Auction Platform, and each Party "will return **or destroy**" the other's Confidential Information. Nothing else in the document addresses exit — searches for data return, export, deletion and transition turned up only security obligations (section 8(iii), p0035) and the general survival language (p0070).

**Why that fails the fallback.** This is a hosted auction-platform deal in which Kubient collects, maintains and stores AP data and receives "Requests" from AP. Yet:
- there is no obligation to **return** AP's data at all — the Confidential Information clause is elective ("return *or* destroy"), and the election sits with the holder, i.e. Kubient;
- no format requirement, no export deadline, no deletion certification;
- no wind-down or transition assistance of any duration.

That is below the fallback (90 days' assistance plus export within 30 days) and edges toward walk-away territory, since Kubient could lawfully destroy AP material on termination without ever handing it back.

**Redline.** A new (v)–(vi) inserted after p0022, inside the existing effects-of-termination list: six months' transition assistance on request at Kubient's then-current rates, return of Content, Requests and other Customer data in a commonly used machine-readable format within 30 days, then deletion with written certification. I used the Agreement's own defined terms ("Content," "Requests") rather than importing an undefined "Customer Data," since that term does not appear in this document.

One drafting note worth flagging to the deal team: the fallback (90 days) is offered in the comment, so the negotiator has room to trade duration without reopening the data-return and certification mechanics, which are the parts that matter most here.
